Trail and Errors: 

My goal was to get all the expenses from each team from each available year together. This was going to be my x-axis (the y-axis was going to be the win% of said teams). However, I struggled to get the totals I wanted. It listed every year in terms of expenses for each team instead of giving me the TOTAL (10 year total) from said teams. That made the graphs messy. With the help of Prof. Willis, he was able to provide me the proper steps to give me what I wanted, and it is reflected in the code below. The dataframe CFB_Total_Expenses reflects what I was seeking and the dataframe CFB_Combined_2015to2024 includes the total expenses along with the winning percentage. The ggplot graph at the end shows the relationship between money and winning.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

The data files are stored alongside this notebook in the repository's
`Final Project` folder. These paths are relative to that folder.
```{r}
CFB_WPCT_2015to2024 <- read_csv(
  "WPCTData.txt",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(Team = str_squish(Team))
```
```{r}
CFP_Expenses_2015to2024 <- read_csv(
  "C:/Users/Owner/Downloads/CFB_Expenses_2015to2024 - Sport_Data_2024_2023_2022_2021_2020_2019_2018_2017_2016_2015 (1).csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  select(`Survey Year`, Team, Expenses) |>
  mutate(
    Team = str_squish(Team),
    Team = recode(
      Team,
      "NC State" = "North Carolina State",
      "TCU" = "Texas Christian",
      "UConn" = "Connecticut",
      "UMass" = "Massachusetts",
      "UNLV" = "Nevada-Las Vegas",
      "Ioa" = "Iowa"
    )
  )
```
## Join winning percentages to annual expenses
The winning-percentage file has one row per team for the entire 2015–2024
period. The expense file has one row per team and survey year. Joining on
`Team` keeps each expense year and repeats the team's full-period winning
percentage; it does not create annual winning percentages. The left join
also retains teams without matching expense data, with missing expense values.

```{r}
CFB_Combined_2015to2024 <- CFB_WPCT_2015to2024 |>
  left_join(
    CFP_Expenses_2015to2024,
    by = "Team",
    relationship = "one-to-many"
  )

glimpse(CFB_Combined_2015to2024)
```

Check which teams do not have expense records:

```{r}
unmatched_teams <- CFB_WPCT_2015to2024 |>
  anti_join(CFP_Expenses_2015to2024, by = "Team") |>
  select(Team)

unmatched_teams
```
Test runs I can do relate mostly to the relationship between money and winning. But looking at the early data, two teams stand out above the others in Boise State and Appalachian State. These two teams rank in the top in terms of total wins from 2015 to 2024, yet will likely rank lower in terms of total expenses. If I could make a chart or some graphic that highlights these two, I would look into that. 

```{r}
# Total each team's expenses across 2015–2024.
CFB_Total_Expenses <- CFP_Expenses_2015to2024 |>
  filter(`Survey Year` %in% 2015:2024) |>
  group_by(Team) |>
  summarize(
    Total_Expenses = if (all(is.na(Expenses))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      sum(Expenses, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    Years_Reported = n_distinct(`Survey Year`[!is.na(Expenses)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  
```

```{r}
CFB_Combined_2015to2024 <- CFB_WPCT_2015to2024 |>
  left_join(
    CFB_Total_Expenses,
    by = "Team",
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
```

```{r}
# Check for incomplete expense histories before comparing totals.
CFB_Combined_2015to2024 |>
  filter(is.na(Years_Reported) | Years_Reported != 10)
  
```

```{r}

# if the W/L column is called W-L%, otherwise fix that
ggplot(
  CFB_Combined_2015to2024,
  aes(x = Total_Expenses, y = `W-L%▼`)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ","
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Total football expenses, 2015–2024 ($)",
    y = "Winning percentage, 2015–2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
